title: Honest Interval Length for Transported Complier Effects under Compliance and Weight Caps
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope

The note proves only a constant-factor frontier for the single critical weight w(x)=1/(2 sqrt(x)), with a known public cap and a separately assumed integrated numerator bridge; it does not establish an exact minimax constant or a general transported-CACE theory.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived matching constant-factor finite-sample bounds for honest connected intervals in the disclosed capped critical-weight IV model, including a legal full-observation lower family and nested-cap nonadaptation. The D0.5 math referee passed without findings, but the cold tier review graded the delivered scope subfield below the required field floor; a closest-result literature comparison also remains incomplete. The exact local experiment and minimax constant remain open, and the prospective application has not been shown to satisfy the model's weight and public-cap assumptions.
tldr: The core theorem establishes matching finite-sample upper and lower bounds, up to constants depending only on \(\alpha\), for the maximal expected length: \(L_n(a,M)\asymp_{\alpha}\min\{1,(M/a)\Omega_{nM^2}(w)\}\), equivalently of order \(\min\{1,\sqrt{\log(e+nM^2)/(na^2)}\}\).
gap: Transported-CACE work supplies identification and regular weighted inference, critical-overlap work supplies truncation rates for weighted means or policy values, and honest-adaptation work supplies abstract modulus bounds. None of the verified sources couples a latent compliance cap, a weak causal ratio, the critical non-square-integrable weight, and divergence control for every observed IV cell.
fill: The project derives the score envelope and its sharp two-sided clipping width from the causal restrictions, constructs a finite-sample honest inversion with explicit endpoint conventions, embeds the matching modulus in legal monotone-IV laws, and quantifies the pointwise price of broader-cap honesty.
